definition.interpretation: The inconclusive result (preference variance ~0.094) suggests that static random Gaussian input noise is insufficient to test for the emergence of stable preferences. The system appears robust or perhaps unresponsive to high-frequency noise, failing to show the clear divergence or convergence expected in true preference formation.
definition.limitations: The current simulation relies on simplistic random inputs which may not model the 'interaction' required for preference emergence. The absence of a feedback loop or goal-oriented objective function limits the system's ability to demonstrate preference stability.
definition.next_step: Define a methodology incorporating structured, non-random perturbations to the input stream to test if preferences stabilize against environmental changes.

definition.uncertainty: The optimal structure of environmental perturbation required to induce stability is currently unknown.
